{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use the existing Spring XD module, stream, container, and module-deployment extension points rather than introducing a separate execution framework.",
    "Implement the Kafka source using Kafka's low-level/simple consumer API, with explicit partition assignment and offset management exposed through module configuration.",
    "Treat the Kafka simple-consumer work as a spike and documented design outcome; production-grade Kafka source implementation beyond the spike is not included unless required by the existing codebase.",
    "Implement custom uber-jar installation through a REST endpoint with upload validation, controlled storage, metadata registration, and an explicit refresh or restart operation as required by the existing container lifecycle.",
    "Implement the generator as a source module with configurable message count, message size, and thread count, using deterministic byte payloads and bounded worker threads.",
    "Implement perf-meter as a sink module that counts messages and writes timestamp, cumulative count, and rate-since-last-report to the standard container log at the configured interval.",
    "Use existing Spring XD stream syntax and the singlenode container for the generator-to-perf-meter performance scenario.",
    "Implement database ingestion around a reusable source abstraction, initially supporting JDBC/database extraction and target adapters for HDFS and HAWQ/GPDB using existing project integration mechanisms where available.",
    "Use JUnit and the repository's established integration-test conventions for Kafka source and sink coverage, with an embedded or test-container Kafka broker where compatible.",
    "Maintain Java 17 compatibility and follow the existing project's build, dependency, logging, configuration, and REST conventions."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing Spring XD source tree, build infrastructure, module SDK, REST layer, and deployment mechanisms are available and build successfully before implementation begins.",
    "The increment is implemented by one software developer; estimates represent active work-hours and exclude elapsed waiting time, staffing overhead, and external approval delays.",
    "U1 is scoped to a production-oriented JDBC/database ingestion path plus HDFS and HAWQ/GPDB target support and an extensible adapter design; support for every possible database or data source is not included.",
    "Existing HDFS and HAWQ/GPDB client libraries or integration patterns can be reused; extensive development of new distributed storage clients is excluded.",
    "The Kafka simple consumer spike includes investigation, a small technical prototype if useful, compatibility analysis, and documentation of findings and next steps, but not a complete production Kafka source and sink rewrite.",
    "Kafka source and sink modules either already exist or require only the test-facing changes needed to make them testable; the estimate includes functional CI coverage, not a full Kafka feature expansion.",
    "REST module upload is limited to authenticated or existing-project-authorized access, basic archive validation, safe file handling, registration, and deployment through the current cluster lifecycle.",
    "The sample application is a GitHub-ready example with configuration and README documentation, not a hosted production deployment.",
    "Generator and perf-meter requirements use the defaults stated in the specification and do not include a new graphical user interface.",
    "Performance validation is a repeatable singlenode test of one million 1,000-byte messages with one thread, rather than a formal benchmark campaign across multiple hardware configurations.",
    "Testing uses available local or CI infrastructure; provisioning a new multi-node cluster or managed Kafka/HDFS environment is excluded.",
    "Documentation covers configuration, usage, design findings, deployment, and test execution sufficiently for maintainers and users."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository analysis and detailed requirements baseline",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing Spring XD modules, build, extension points, REST services, Kafka integration, deployment lifecycle, logging conventions, and test infrastructure; convert the user stories into implementable acceptance criteria.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Increment architecture and design",
      "activity_description": "Design the database-ingestion abstraction and target adapters, Kafka spike boundaries, custom-module upload flow, generator and perf-meter configuration, sample application structure, and CI test strategy.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Database ingestion modules",
      "activity_description": "Implement and integrate the scoped JDBC/database ingestion flow, configurable extraction and batching, error handling, and HDFS plus HAWQ/GPDB target adapters using existing Spring XD module and storage integration points.",
      "most_likely_effort": 96
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Kafka simple consumer API spike",
      "activity_description": "Study the low-level Kafka consumer behavior, partition assignment, offset control, rebalance implications, failure handling, and compatibility with the existing framework; produce a documented recommendation, prototype findings, and next steps.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "REST API for custom uber-jar installation",
      "activity_description": "Implement the upload endpoint and supporting validation, storage, metadata registration, deployment or refresh integration, error responses, logging, and REST-level tests for installing custom modules in the cluster.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Kafka sample application and GitHub project",
      "activity_description": "Create a runnable reference application showing Kafka as the message bus and Kafka as a source, including cluster provisioning configuration, stream definitions, dependency setup, README instructions, and troubleshooting notes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Generator source module",
      "activity_description": "Implement the configurable generator source with message count, payload size, and thread count options, default handling, lifecycle behavior, concurrency controls, validation, unit tests, and module packaging.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Perf-meter sink module",
      "activity_description": "Implement message counting and configurable reporting intervals, calculate rate since the prior report, emit timestamp/count/rate records to the standard container log, and add validation and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Generator-to-perf-meter stream and performance scenario",
      "activity_description": "Configure and validate the generator | perf-meter stream in a singlenode container, execute the one-million-message and 1,000-byte payload scenario, resolve integration issues, and record reproducible usage and observed measurements.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Kafka source and sink automated test coverage",
      "activity_description": "Add unit and integration tests for Kafka source and sink behavior, including message flow, configuration, partition or offset behavior relevant to the spike, error cases, and broker setup suitable for CI.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Cross-module testing and defect resolution",
      "activity_description": "Add focused tests for ingestion, REST upload, generator, perf-meter, and stream wiring; execute the complete test suite, diagnose failures, and fix implementation or integration defects.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "User and maintainer documentation",
      "activity_description": "Document module configuration, database ingestion examples, REST upload usage, generator and perf-meter commands, Kafka spike conclusions, sample project operation, and performance-test execution.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "Build and CI integration",
      "activity_description": "Update build descriptors, dependencies, packaging, test profiles, CI service configuration, artifacts, and verification steps so the new modules and Kafka coverage execute reliably in continuous integration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 480
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring XD module, stream, container, and module-deployment extension points rather than introducing a separate execution framework.
Implement the Kafka source using Kafka's low-level/simple consumer API, with explicit partition assignment and offset management exposed through module configuration.
Treat the Kafka simple-consumer work as a spike and documented design outcome; production-grade Kafka source implementation beyond the spike is not included unless required by the existing codebase.

Implement custom uber-jar installation through a REST endpoint with upload validation, controlled storage, metadata registration, and an explicit refresh or restart operation as required by the existing container lifecycle.
Implement the generator as a source module with configurable message count, message size, and thread count, using deterministic byte payloads and bounded worker threads.
Implement perf-meter as a sink module that counts messages and writes timestamp, cumulative count, and rate-since-last-report to the standard container log at the configured interval.
Use existing Spring XD stream syntax and the singlenode container for the generator-to-perf-meter performance scenario.

Implement database ingestion around a reusable source abstraction, initially supporting JDBC/database extraction and target adapters for HDFS and HAWQ/GPDB using existing project integration mechanisms where available.
Use JUnit and the repository's established integration-test conventions for Kafka source and sink coverage, with an embedded or test-container Kafka broker where compatible.
Maintain Java 17 compatibility and follow the existing project's build, dependency, logging, configuration, and REST conventions.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD source tree, build infrastructure, module SDK, REST layer, and deployment mechanisms are available and build successfully before implementation begins.
The increment is implemented by one software developer; estimates represent active work-hours and exclude elapsed waiting time, staffing overhead, and external approval delays.

U1 is scoped to a production-oriented JDBC/database ingestion path plus HDFS and HAWQ/GPDB target support and an extensible adapter design; support for every possible database or data source is not included.
Existing HDFS and HAWQ/GPDB client libraries or integration patterns can be reused; extensive development of new distributed storage clients is excluded.

The Kafka simple consumer spike includes investigation, a small technical prototype if useful, compatibility analysis, and documentation of findings and next steps, but not a complete production Kafka source and sink rewrite.

Kafka source and sink modules either already exist or require only the test-facing changes needed to make them testable; the estimate includes functional CI coverage, not a full Kafka feature expansion.
REST module upload is limited to authenticated or existing-project-authorized access, basic archive validation, safe file handling, registration, and deployment through the current cluster lifecycle.
The sample application is a GitHub-ready example with configuration and README documentation, not a hosted production deployment.
Generator and perf-meter requirements use the defaults stated in the specification and do not include a new graphical user interface.
Performance validation is a repeatable singlenode test of one million 1,000-byte messages with one thread, rather than a formal benchmark campaign across multiple hardware configurations.
Testing uses available local or CI infrastructure; provisioning a new multi-node cluster or managed Kafka/HDFS environment is excluded.
Documentation covers configuration, usage, design findings, deployment, and test execution sufficiently for maintainers and users.
